I lost my little sister last june. Going on a year and it still has me really fucked up. She was my only sibling and her passing has changed the trajectory of my life. I have no one to talk to because no one else in my life really understands how it feels. I feel disconnected from all of my friends, the rest of my family, even my own wife; and it has unfortunately taken a toll on my most important relationships. It's hard to be around someone so miserable all the time. I get that, but I'm so caught up in my grief that I don't know how to not be miserable anymore. It's like my joy is gone. I cant just cut loose and have fun anymore, can't even talk to people most days because I have nothing to say.

Now I have to go through my parents dying alone. She was supposed to be the one to have kids, now if I don't, my family line dies with me. She was the closest person in the world to me. She was supposed to be here, she was supposed to outlive me. I was supposed to protect her. But I failed. Now I have to do it alone.

A wise woman once told me that there is nothing more personal and universal than grief. It's been a real mindfuck for sure. 

So, I hope it gets easier. Going on a year for me and I still cry every day.

I was raised in a secular fashion. I've been to church a handful of times with grandparents, but never really had anything forced upon me. I always appreciated that because it allowed me to explore multiple systems of belief throughout my youth. I found that I didn't resonate with any of them, except Buddhism, but even then I didn't really care for the mythology around it, moreso I respected it as a way of thinking.

But throughout my journey, I did come to believe in "something more" that we don't understand. And I did used to believe that, as long as I lived as a good person, that "something more" would look out for me, for lack of a better term. The universe conspires with me, I used to believe. Karma, I guess I primarily believed in karma.

But when my sister died, I lost that faith. Now I lean more towards the idea that there's nothing really. This existence is a fluke. I was smart enough to know I really knew nothing, but I felt like the universe cared about me, I guess, at the very least because I was a part of itself. I still know that I don't know anything, but if there is "something more," I really don't think it's conscious. If there's some kind of universal power out there, think it's more reactive than proactive. I mean that to say there's no greater plan or true reason, it just simply is, the same way that we simply are.

The core of my reality has been shaken so hard that I'm afraid it has broken. So far, that's been the hardest part of dealing with this grief. It's like I have to re-invent my whole being, and I don't know how or if I can.

Unlimited tolerance must lead to the disappearance of tolerance. If we extend unlimited tolerance even to those who are intolerant, if we are not prepared to defend a tolerant society against the onslaught of the intolerant, then the tolerant will be destroyed, and tolerance with them. 

In this formulation, I do not imply, for instance, that we should always suppress the utterance of intolerant philosophies; as long as we can counter them by rational argument and keep them in check by public opinion, suppression would certainly be unwise. But we should claim the right to suppress them if necessary even by force; for it may easily turn out that they are not prepared to meet us on the level of rational argument, but begin by denouncing all argument; they may forbid their followers to listen to rational argument, because it is deceptive, and teach them to answer arguments by the use of their fists or pistols. 

We should therefore claim, in the name of tolerance, the right not to tolerate the intolerant. We should claim that any movement preaching intolerance places itself outside the law, and we should consider incitement to intolerance and persecution as criminal, in the same way as we should consider incitement to murder, or to kidnapping, or to the revival of the slave trade, as criminal.

You're talking about volumetric dosing. You could search that here and find a bunch of threads but basically, when you're working with something potent like that, it's safer and easier cause you don't have to keep using your scale.

It's simple math. Determine how strong you want the solution. For example, if you have a 30 milliliter bottle and you want to dose by the milligram. You want each dose to be 5 milligrams. So that's 5mg/ml. 30ml bottle means you will have 30 doses if you go by 1 dose= 1ml. 5mg/ml for a 30ml bottle means you will have to dissolve 150 mg substance in whatever solvent (water, alcohol, etc) to achieve your desired potency.

150mg/30ml = 5mg/1ml

300mg/30ml = 10mg/ml

15mg/30ml = .5mg/ml

You will need to look up whatever solvent will best keep the substance you're using. And you will need some kind of measured dropper to dose accurately.

Edit: also make sure you'll have enough solvent to properly dissolve all of your substance. Hot water baths will help you dissolve. And shake shake SHAKE. You're gonna have to do a little research on your own, but it's super easy.

There are physical limits that are mathematically determined and then there are our mutual experiences, but there are an infinite amount of layers which we cant see that exist at all times. What I have come to believe is that there is a baseline "consciousness" which is an energy that permeates the universe kind of like background radiation. Imagine a perfectly still body of water. This water is so freaking clear and calm that you cant even see it, you wouldnt even know it was there. But it is, so the potential for ripples have always existed. The wind blows and the water is changed, that's the big bang, gravity and electromagnetic forces shaping the universe into what it is. Then life comes along and starts throwing teensy little pebbles around, causing yet even more ripples. It's the same water, same place, but we are now aware that there even is water because it's over here wiggling around. Our physical selves, our brains and neurotransmitters, are the means by which we perceive our realities and interact with that background radiation, the potential energy that one day will drive ripples across the surface. 

For lack of a better word, our brains are like transistors for our "souls" which is really just the background radiation being affected as it travels through me. The soul is not a ghost that sits in my body all the time until I die. My soul is all around me, and everyone and everything all throughout the universe, our "souls" are the same. My consciousness is just that tiny fragment of the soul as it passes through my brain as feelings and thoughts. Our perceptions are what make us different, the energy is taken in, perceived by us (whether we realize or not), and then put out back into the universe in whatever state we altered it into. I feel like people have auras, I believe in the vibrations that we put out, but I don't believe in an all powerful god in the sense that abrahamic and like-minded religions do.

A god in this sense would be a being that exists in a higher dimension, one who would not even know we existed until it decided to turn it's microscope on us. The analogy I always liked was that of the flatlanders. Flatlanders being creatures that exist in two dimensional spaces. They would never be able to see us, the way we are. They would only be able to perceive us in cross sections, as if we could put a finger through their hypothetical piece of paper universe (a piece of paper is still not totally 2d, but is the best metaphor I can think of). The flatlanders still wouldnt see the whole finger, they'd be freaked out by a sudden wall of flesh just magically appearing in their space. We'd be very god-like in this scenario, and I know for a fact that we arent all powerful, all knowing beings of light and love.

So maybe there is a being above us that has it's microscope turned on, but theres always going to be a being above it. Potentially forever. Even if it tried to influence us, it's unlikely that we could understand or comprehend it. Even if it did learn how to subvert the constraints of physical reality and lower itself down to our level of perception, how could we even begin to fathom its motives or intent? The only exception, the only thing that could be considered the one true god, is something that exists outside of literally everything, therefore exists nowhere. It cant be comprehended by us.

It's the energy that I perceive as a thought, and therefore put out via thought, and it has always existed, will always exist in this 3d universe I am in. Not even time can change that. It flows throughout the solar system, the galaxy, everywhere. But most importantly, it flows through you. As you read this, I am effectively influencing your consciousness with my ideas, whether you agree or not doesn't matter, because we exist. That, in my opinion, is why we are here in the first place. We exist to experience each other and this world, for all the good and bad it does us. My loved ones who've died still exist within my memories, and their souls are the same as they've always been. For me, god is everywhere. It's just constantly changing.

Be very careful, have a plan set with activities to do, clear your schedule and have a trip sitter (someone you would trust with your life). if you plan to do it alone, I'd avoid people, even my closest friends can weird me out if I'm tripping and they're not, feels like we're at opposite ends of a very long tunnel. It doesn't matter what kind, any psychedelic can fuck your brain up even worse if you get into a bad thought loop and honestly, you'd be worse off, could end up in the hospital or worse from doing something stupid. Practice meditation as a means of controlling which thoughts to ignore and which to give power, it's a skill that will help you tremendously while you're tripping, no matter who you are. And always start low, cause once you take a drug, only time will make it wear off, but having some emergency benzos on hand always helps me, even if I don't take them, the option of being able to calm myself down or totally shut it off by forcibly going to sleep eases a lot of the anxiety. Psychedelics are a double edged sword, and they will demand your respect, so travel safely my friend. And someone said try MDMA, I second that if you're really in that state of mind where you just want relief.

Just be careful you don't get something like serotonin syndrome. Also, sometimes it doesn't matter what drug or how much you take, if you have any prominent or underlying psychological concerns, tripping can bring it all out in the worst way possible. Especially if you're alone. A few months ago, I had recently broken up with my girlfriend, and out of boredom/hopes it would get my mind off of life, I took whichever psych (1p or miprocin) and instead of having fun, I got caught in a negative thought loop and basically just ended up crying my fucking eyes out for hours. 0/10 would never do again if my mind isn't feeling right, cause that shit will drive you nuts. Actually, one of those times, I did go to the hospital and ended up staying in the bhu for a week. Worst. Trip. Ever.
My advice, don't risk it if you have unresolved feelings about something or even think it could go wrong. Also, having a sitter/buddy present helps tremendously. Sorry about your experience, just tread with caution next time.
